Name: neorv32_cpu_control.debug_ctrl.run
Structural Path: debug_ctrl.run -> debug execution control -> privilege-control path -> ctrl_o.lsu_priv
Attack Scenarios: Manipulating neorv32_cpu_control.debug_ctrl.run through an untrusted control can corrupt debug execution control -> privilege-control path, allowing an otherwise disallowed operation to affect ctrl_o.lsu_priv.
Justification: A false debug-run state changes the privilege/control context and showed the strongest authorization-bypass response.

Name: neorv32_cpu_control.csr.prv_level
Attack Scenarios: Manipulating neorv32_cpu_control.csr.prv_level through an untrusted control can corrupt effective-privilege selection, allowing an otherwise disallowed operation to affect ctrl_o.lsu_priv.
Justification: The current privilege level directly contributes to effective LSU privilege and is both reachable and bypass-sensitive.

Name: neorv32_cpu_control.csr.mstatus_mpp
Attack Scenarios: Manipulating neorv32_cpu_control.csr.mstatus_mpp through an untrusted control can corrupt MPRV privilege mux, allowing an otherwise disallowed operation to affect ctrl_o.lsu_priv.
Justification: MPP supplies the effective privilege for MPRV accesses; corruption can turn a denied user access into an elevated one.

Name: neorv32_cpu_control.csr.mstatus_mprv
Attack Scenarios: Manipulating neorv32_cpu_control.csr.mstatus_mprv through an untrusted control can corrupt effective-privilege selection, allowing an otherwise disallowed operation to affect ctrl_o.lsu_priv.
Justification: MPRV selects whether M-mode data accesses inherit MPP, making it a direct authorization control.

Name: neorv32_cpu_control.ctrl.csr_we
Structural Path: ctrl.csr_we -> privilege CSR update -> effective-privilege selection -> ctrl_o.lsu_priv
Attack Scenarios: Manipulating neorv32_cpu_control.ctrl.csr_we through an untrusted control can corrupt privilege CSR update -> effective-privilege selection, allowing an otherwise disallowed operation to affect ctrl_o.lsu_priv.
Justification: A spurious CSR write can modify the privilege state that feeds LSU authorization.

Name: neorv32_cpu_control.ctrl_nxt.csr_we
Structural Path: ctrl_nxt.csr_we -> registered ctrl.csr_we -> privilege CSR update -> effective-privilege selection -> ctrl_o.lsu_priv
Attack Scenarios: Manipulating the next-cycle CSR-write authorization can create an unauthorized privilege-CSR update that changes the effective LSU privilege.
Justification: This is the sampled next-state authorization control for privilege-changing CSR writes.

Name: neorv32_cpu_frontend.ipb_rdata(0)
Structural Path: ipb_rdata(0) -> instruction decode -> CSR operation/write control -> privilege CSR state -> ctrl_o.lsu_priv
Attack Scenarios: Unauthorized influence over the fetched instruction halfword can convert the decoded operation into a privilege-changing CSR command.
Justification: The fetched instruction encoding causally controls the CSR operation that can update effective privilege state.

Name: neorv32_cpu.frontend.i32
Structural Path: frontend.i32 -> instruction decode -> CSR address/data/write control -> privilege CSR state -> ctrl_o.lsu_priv
Attack Scenarios: Corrupting the assembled 32-bit instruction can synthesize an unauthorized CSR write that changes MPRV or MPP.
Justification: The assembled instruction is the canonical decoded command source for privilege-changing CSR operations.

Name: neorv32_cpu_frontend.ipb_rdata(1)
Structural Path: ipb_rdata(1) -> instruction assembly/decode -> CSR operation/write control -> privilege CSR state -> ctrl_o.lsu_priv
Attack Scenarios: Unauthorized influence over the second fetched halfword can change the decoded CSR address or operands and cause a privilege-changing operation.
Justification: This instruction halfword supplies decoded fields that control privilege-changing CSR operations.

Name: neorv32_cpu_control.env_exit
Structural Path: env_exit -> privilege restoration (csr.prv_level/csr.mstatus_mpp) -> effective-privilege selection -> ctrl_o.lsu_priv
Attack Scenarios: A spurious or mistimed environment-exit transition can restore an attacker-chosen saved privilege and elevate the effective LSU access privilege.
Justification: Retained by explicit expert mechanism adjudication: environment return directly changes privilege state even though the measured bypass set did not activate it. The measured threat evidence is weak because bypass sensitivity is zero, but SecID retains it for the direct, security-specific privilege-restoration mechanism.

Name: neorv32_cpu.ctrl.csr_wdata
Structural Path: ctrl.csr_wdata -> mstatus CSR write -> csr.mstatus_mpp/csr.mstatus_mprv -> ctrl_o.lsu_priv
Attack Scenarios: Unauthorized modification of CSR write data can set MPP or MPRV during a legal mstatus write and thereby elevate effective LSU privilege.
Justification: The canonical CSR write-data signal directly supplies the privilege bits written into mstatus; its mechanism is strong despite zero activation in the measured bypass scenarios.
